study.title: Deep learning-based frame synthesis enables radiation dose reduction in digital subtraction angiography imaging: a multicenter study

imaging.modality_detail: 2D-DSA (planar, fixed C-arm position) and 3D rotational DSA (continuous 180-degree C-arm rotation)
imaging.territory_detail: Cerebral DSA (head and neck), with some thorax sequences; IA, CVS, AVM, AVF, moyamoya disease

data_released.detail: Only reader responses/scores provided as Supplementary Data; no image data release stated

annotation.annotator_expertise: Interventional radiologists with 10-15 years of experience (visual Turing test and quality ratings; real frames serve as ground truth)
annotation.inter_rater_value: Turing test Fleiss' kappa 0.020-0.126 (1-6 frames), 0.108 (3D); quality rating kappa as low as 0.454 (2D AVF); diagnostic confidence kappa 0.645-1.000 for generated sequences

task.task_description: Intermediate frame synthesis (video frame interpolation) in 2D and 3D DSA sequences from sparsely acquired real frames, generating up to 6 frames between real frames to reduce radiation dose to 1/7.
task.clinical_application: Radiation dose reduction in cerebrovascular DSA imaging for diagnosis and interventional neuroradiology

temporal_evidence.quote: The FGFS module combined a bidirectional optical flow estimation network with a feature refinement sub-network, enabling the synthesis of intermediate frame features across multiple scales.

method.pretraining: Pretrained ResNet34 features used for feature-space loss; model trained at 128x128 then fine-tuned on 512x512 crops

evaluation.external_validation_detail: Dataset 2: 3,255 DSA sequences from two external hospitals (GE Medical Systems and Philips Azurion 5M20), used exclusively for external evaluation

metrics.task: guidewire position fidelity in generated 2D thorax sequence
reader quality assessment of generated sequences
reader diagnostic confidence of generated sequences

metrics.metric: Visual Turing test Fleiss' kappa (1-6 frames)
metrics.task: real vs generated discrimination by radiologists

metrics.metric: Visual Turing test Fleiss' kappa (3D sequences)
metrics.task: real vs generated discrimination by radiologists, 3D-DSA

metrics.metric: Visual Turing test Fleiss' kappa (AV-shunt cases)
metrics.task: real vs generated discrimination by radiologists, AV-shunts

metrics.metric: SSIM (2D IA / CVS / AVM, diseases excluded from training)
PSNR (2D IA / CVS / AVM, diseases excluded from training)
SSIM (3D IA / CVS / AVM, diseases excluded from training)
PSNR (3D IA / CVS / AVM, diseases excluded from training)

G2.quote: This dataset was used exclusively for external evaluation to assess the generalizability of the proposed model across different scanner manufacturers.

G3.quote: existing deep learning methods often achieve only modest dose reductions and frequently suffer from inter-frame discontinuity, limiting their clinical applicability

G4.quote: solving the problem of dynamic vascular overlap in 3D rotational sequences and ensuring the anatomical fidelity of generated frames

G6.quote: it has not yet been evaluated on real-world clinical tasks

other_limitations: Lower scores and Kappa coefficients for some disease types in clinical assessment
Fails to remove artifacts or reconstruct vessels when all input frames contain severe artifacts
Artifact suppression may introduce mild blurring in some frames
No formal diagnostic consistency metrics prospectively defined
future_work: Incorporate data with more complex vascular structures
Extend to more anatomical regions such as heart and limbs
Evaluate generated sequences on downstream tasks such as IA segmentation and CVS detection
